candidate.title: Ψ -seq / PSI-seq
candidate.scope: Assigned third row of the attached poster: Ψ-seq / PSI-seq, captioned Pseudouridine identification sequencing (PSI-seq and Ψ-seq), from poly(A)-selected, DNase-treated RNA to purified cDNA. These are distinct named assays grouped around CMC-dependent RT-stop detection, not established aliases or interchangeable complete protocols. The w_ route preserves all five drawn transformations and their treatment-before-fragmentation history; the primary Ψ-seq workflow supports that order. The separate l_ route is an explicitly primary-supported resolution for the grouped PSI-seq member: fragmentation precedes CMCT/alkaline treatment. It reuses the depicted purposes, with distinct local operations and states; it is not a second drawn lane, sample split, pooling event or unshown adaptation. The catalogue page heading and schematic identify PSI-seq, so that page supports PSI-seq context only. Adjacent MeRIP/m6A, miCLIP and Pseudo-seq rows are outside the assigned target; the pseudouridine-residue icon is a substrate key, not an additional operation. Mock/IVT controls, experimental conditions, complete sequencing-library finishing and computational analysis are not added as graph branches. The papers clarify how the recovered cDNA can report Ψ positions and where the common drawing abbreviates member-specific preparation.

operations.label: CMC treatment and OH− treatment
operations.description: Chemically treat the prepared long RNA, then apply the depicted alkaline treatment. The output is RNA bearing persistent CMC adducts at Ψ sites, represented by orange pendants; the endogenous Ψ sites themselves were present in the input.
operations.mechanism: CMC reacts with U, G and Ψ; alkaline treatment hydrolyzes the less stable U/G adducts while N3-CMC–Ψ is relatively stable. CMC and OH− are reagents for this combined local operation.
operations.information_effect: Creates a chemical obstacle that can convert a biological RNA modification into a reverse-transcription termination signal. Retention after chemical treatment is not itself proof of perfect biological specificity.
